x: Our "D" team (Wright, Readman, Goold and Earle) took the first handicap team prizes, and so we can consider we had our share.
Elson, Brian, Readman, Goold and Boddington (to mention a few) would have fared, had it been possible for them to turn out.

Elson, Heather, Goold, Jarvis, Boddington, Snell Hamer, Spooner, Cornish, Joe Coleman, Earle, Urry, Clark, Pattenden, Willis, True and several others, some beginners, who are showing rapid improvement.

Clayton, Heather, Roberts, Thaxter, Doubleday, Bridger, Goold, Elliott, East, Snell and others have great potentialities, and with conscientious, steady training, we may expect a team which will represent the Club with credit.

The war has been responsible for bringing many of our older members out of retirement, and in this respite we welcome back, among others: Charlie Redgrave, Jarvis Boddington, Willis, Ted Jackman, and Goold.

A Club Handicap was held in conjunction, and once again young Mac managed to pull it off, with Doub (walking again) 2nd and Stan Goold 3rd. In January Surrey A.C. came to Wimbledon with a strong team and just managed to beat us by one point, the score being 85 point to 86.
